::: {.lead-large}
A field guide for colleagues to one specific way of using LLMs:
**giving an AI agent direct access to your project files** so it can write
code, edit your LaTeX, audit a replication package, and run things on your
behalf — under your supervision.

This is not about chatting with ChatGPT in a browser. That is useful too,
but it isn't what changed in the last year.
:::

## Suggested reading order

If you have **30 minutes**:

1. [Principles](principles.qmd) — the three things that determine how
   useful Claude Code will be for you.
2. [What is agentic coding?](big-picture/what-is-agentic.qmd) — what it
   means and why it's different from chatting with an LLM (five minutes).
3. [Install Claude Code](getting-started/install.qmd), then
   [use it inside VS Code](getting-started/vscode.qmd) — recommended if
   you're coming from RStudio, Stata, or Matlab. (Never used the terminal?
   The [terminal primer](getting-started/terminal-and-bash.qmd) is helpful
   background even on the VS Code route.)
4. A worked example: [editing a LaTeX paper](examples/latex-paper.qmd) or
   [auditing a replication package](examples/replication-package.qmd).

If you have **a free afternoon**, add:

5. [Plan mode, todos, slash commands](getting-started/plan-mode-and-todo.qmd).
6. The example page for your language: Stata, R, or Julia.
7. [How to ask](workflow/how-to-ask.qmd) and
   [verifying output](workflow/verifying.qmd) — how to ask well and when
   to check the result.
8. The pitfalls, before letting Claude touch anything serious:
   [confidential data](pitfalls/confidential-data.qmd),
   [hallucinations](pitfalls/hallucinations.qmd), and
   [what you must still do yourself](pitfalls/judgment.qmd).

## Work in progress

The two long-form examples (LaTeX paper editing and replication-package
audit), the install guide, and the Git and terminal primers are the most
complete pages. Others are short outlines for now. If a section would help
you and isn't there yet, email me — that's the fastest way to set the
priority.
